articles.headline: Florida flips nation's No. 1 2027 receiver from Texas
keyFacts: Five-star wide receiver Easton Royal flipped his commitment from Texas to the Florida Gators on Sunday, according to the Royal family.
Royal ranks as the nation's number one wide receiver and number eight overall recruit in the ESPN 300.
Royal is expected to cancel scheduled visits to Texas and LSU and shut down his recruitment following a longstanding relationship with head coach Jon Sumrall.
body: The Florida Gators scored a major recruiting victory by flipping five-star wide receiver Easton Royal from Texas on Sunday. Head coach Jon Sumrall's inaugural recruiting class gets a major boost while delivering a significant blow to the Longhorns' 2027 plans. The Royal family confirmed the decision to ESPN on Sunday.

The 6-foot, 205-pound prospect from New Orleans ranks as the nation's No. 1 wide receiver and No. 8 overall recruit in the SC Next ESPN 300. He initially committed to Texas last November, becoming the first player in the Longhorns' 2027 recruiting class. The decision followed Royal's latest visit to Florida, which came during the Gators' 38-19 loss to South Carolina on Saturday.

After months of interest from several SEC powerhouse programs, Royal is expected to cancel his scheduled visits to Texas and LSU and shut down his recruitment. Sumrall's longstanding relationship with Royal played a crucial role in the flip. He first offered Royal while coaching at Tulane in March 2025 and continued pursuing him after taking over at Florida late last year.

Royal previously praised Sumrall's achievements, saying he viewed the coach as a winner following his success at Tulane. That relationship ultimately helped Florida overcome competing offers and secure one of the country's most coveted prospects.

He becomes Florida's second highest-rated recruit in the 2027 class, joining five-star offensive tackle Maxwell Hiller, who is ranked No. 7 nationally, and quarterback Davin Davidson, ESPN's No. 6 pocket passer.

Florida entered Saturday with the nation's No. 8 recruiting class. If Royal signs in December, he would represent the program's highest-ranked wide receiver addition since Percy Harvin in 2006. The Louisiana native brings exceptional athleticism and production. He recorded 2,095 all-purpose yards and 29 total touchdowns during his junior season.
In May, he also won a state championship and set a Louisiana record in the 100-meter dash with a time of 10.17 seconds, breaking a mark that had stood for 46 years.
Royal's flip could reshape the 2027 recruiting race while adding renewed momentum in "The Swamp" despite consecutive losses.

articles.headline: Bengals safety reveals Malik Willis 'tell' that led to two interceptions by Dolphins QB
keyFacts: Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle stated publicly that Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis had a physical tell before throwing the ball.
Battle intercepted Willis twice during the game, helping the Bengals snap their two-game losing streak.
Some critics argued Battle should not have revealed the information publicly before the game.
body: With the Miami Dolphins off to a slow start, opposing teams are looking at the team as a chance for an easy win. The Cincinnati Bengals, for one, were able to get off their two-game losing streak, with a lot of help from a safety who figured out new Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis.

Bengals defender Jordan Battle revealed during the week that the defense could recognize when Willis was going to throw the ball based on a "tell" that the quarterback had. Then, Battle backed up his words with a big day on defense, as he was responsible for two of the Bengals three forced turnovers.

While some believed Battle was wrong to reveal his information to the media, it didn't matter much as the Bengals defense had a great day in Miami. Here's how Battle used his information on Willis to produce a big day on the field.
Jordan Battle revealed Malik Willis tell
During the week, Bengals safety Jordan Battle told the media that Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis had a "tell" that would help the defense.

"He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that that gives the read the break."

Jordan Battle on Malik Willis: “He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball. He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that that gives the read the break. He's obviously dangerous with his feet. We know we got to be alert for that. Third and longs, they will run quarterback draws, and in the passing game, he will extend plays. So we got to be good downfield. DBs are plastering, so we got to be alert for that. He will take chances. We just got to be on, be alert on guys where they line up.”

articles.headline: Hits & Misses: Anderson and Wirtz offering opposite value for money
keyFacts: Manchester City defeated Liverpool 3-0, with pundits praising Elliot Anderson as a bargain and noting Florian Wirtz struggled to make an impact.
Crystal Palace achieved a 3-1 comeback win over Nottingham Forest, showing signs of improved attacking form under manager Pierre Sage.
Everton drew 2-2 with Hull City, and analysts stated that the club needs to sign another striker in January to sustain a push for European qualification.
body: Man City's Elliot Anderson deemed a bargain while Florian Wirtz fails to offer return on Liverpool's huge investment - Premier League hits and misses

Sky Sports' football writers analyse Sunday's Premier League action as Florian Wirtz shrinks on the big occasion again, but Elliot Anderson shines; Crystal Palace spoil Oliver Glasner's Selhurst Park return; Everton missing clinical edge to become European contenders
Sunday 11 October 2026 20:28, UK
Manchester City's siege mentality won out at Liverpool. Their quality with a man over telling, if not quite so obvious when both sides had a full complement of players for an hour of the game.
Absolutely everything good about City in their 3-0 win was summed up by the classy performance of Elliot Anderson.

Not for the first time since his mega-money move from Nottingham Forest, the midfielder's mastery on the ball was matched by his maturity off it. A "bargain" at £116m, according to Jamie Carragher, every bit capable, in his own way, of exerting as much control and influence on games as Rodri did in this role.

While the spotlight shines ever brighter on City as a club, and forensics pour over their spending, Anderson remains the picture of calm. Everything a manager would want in a modern-day holding midfielder: a robust runner, aggressive tackler and clever distributor. "He dominates big games," says Gary Neville.

Rarely fazed by the occasion, Anderson has won at Anfield two years running - with two different sides. Of course the way Forest went about success last term shared few similarities with City's more technical display. The only common denominator? Elliot Anderson.
Laura Hunter

Florian Wirtz played his part with the pressing and the constant movement that was a hallmark of Liverpool's up-tempo approach that made life so difficult for Manchester City for an hour at Anfield. But that bit of magic that the supporters wanted was missing.

Rayan Cherki provided that for City's third and final goal, by which point Wirtz was sat on the Liverpool bench having been substituted. Another big game in which the Germany international was unable to provide the spark for his side.

Too many loose touches and loose passes, one or two tackles shirked. Victor Munoz and Lewis Koumas are easy for supporters to embrace with their bustling styles but Wirtz is a player who glides across the turf and he needs end product to justify his role.

There was one shot lashed wide with the game goalless and better options to his left. It is no goals for Wirtz this season and just one in his last 16 Premier League appearances. Another opportunity missed for a classy player still seemingly unable to impose himself.
Adam Bate

Crystal Palace have shown signs of rediscovering their attacking spark under Pierre Sage, with their 3-1 comeback win over Nottingham Forest the latest example.
The Eagles have now scored three or more goals in two of their last four league games - as often as they managed across their previous 37 Premier League matches combined.
Goals and entertaining football were a problem during Oliver Glasner's latter days in charge, as Palace struggled to balance their domestic and European commitments.

There is an early sense of a throwback to the more free-scoring side that flourished under the Austrian in his first season, when their pace, movement and attacking combinations made them a threat to anyone.

It is still early in Sage's tenure, and two high-scoring performances do not guarantee a lasting change. But Palace look to be playing with greater freedom and confidence, with Daichi Kamada, Jefferson Lerma and Yeremy Pino all finding the net against Forest.
If Sage can sustain that attacking momentum while tightening up a defence that has been vulnerable this season, there are encouraging signs of a more dangerous Palace taking shape.
William Bitibiri
Everton are unbeaten after six matches for just the third time in the Premier League era. In 2006/07 and 2013/14 they finished sixth and then fifth from this position.
It is a testament to the hard work of David Moyes, who has returned to challenging circumstances in his second Everton spell, that he has got the club back to looking upwards.
For the last five seasons, Everton have been in the bottom half, often battling relegation. Now, it seems, they have a genuine chance to push up the table and dare to dream bigger.

However, it is hard to see how Moyes can drag them into Europe with Thierno Barry as his only striker. The 23-year-old scored in the end in the 2-2 draw at Hull, but, according to Opta, he needed five big chances to find the back of the net. At least two of those had to go in.
If Everton are to qualify for Europe, they will need a striker who wins them points. At Hull, you could argue they had a striker who cost them points.

Barry, who is Everton's top scorer since the start of last season in the Premier League (11 goals), is improving all the time, but the current situation is unfair on him and his manager. Right now he cannot be depended on consistently.

The Frenchman, who has started all eight of Everton's matches this season, appeared to pull up with cramp towards the end at Hull and Moyes had no choice but to replace him with Charly Alcaraz, who is a midfielder by trade.
There was only four minutes plus stoppage time to go, but it almost felt as if Everton were forced to give up on chasing a late winner. This was a match that was there for the taking.
The plan, of course, was to have Folarin Balogun in the squad. However, his move from Monaco collapsed at the last minute on Deadline Day.

The obvious solution would be to go back in for a striker in January. It remains to be seen how the uncertainty at ownership level will impact their plans. Moyes needs - and deserves - another striker to have a proper chance at a push for Europe.
Zinny Boswell
Mohamed Belloumi is making the difference for Hull City - even when he is tired.

The Algeria winger was benched for the first time this season against Everton after telling head coach Sergej Jakirovic on Friday that he was fatigued after playing three times for his country during the international break.

Belloumi still made a crucial impact on Sunday, netting Hull's equaliser to earn them a point. He has been pivotal in the club's good start, scoring or assisting five of their eight Premier League goals this season.

The 24-year-old was signed from Portuguese side Farense in August 2024 and scored only five goals in 35 Championship appearances over two seasons, but, at a higher level, his pace and fearless dribbling has made a significant contribution already.
Belloumi will return to being the first name on their teamsheet at Fulham next weekend and, if his early-season form is anything to go by, defences will have plenty more to worry about.
David Richardson

articles.headline: Why new Lakers forward can’t contain excitement playing with Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves
keyFacts: Sixth-year forward Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 19 points off the bench in the Lakers preseason win against the Sacramento Kings.
Mamukelashvili said he is excited to play alongside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves because their gravity will create open shots for him.
Head coach JJ Redick stated he plans to use Mamukelashvili's versatility and shooting threat in specialized plays throughout the season.
body: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Why new Lakers forward can’t contain excitement playing with Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

LOS ANGELES – While the Los Angeles Lakers are still juggling their rotation in the midst of preseason and training camp, one player who has locked down his spot is sixth-year forward Sandro Mamukelashvili. The Georgian native shined bright during the team’s preseason victory against the Sacramento Kings this past Thursday, showing his versatility and strong fit alongside the Lakers’ plethora of ball-handlers.

Mamukelashvili finished with 19 points off the bench to go along with three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one blocked shot. He shot 7-of-10 from the field and 3-of-6 from 3-point range. One of the main things he’s looking forward to is the amount of open shots he’ll receive with playing with Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves.

“Yeah, there’s plenty of them. I think there will be even more. When Luka has the ball, you see everybody on their toes defensively. Everybody wants to make sure he gets off it, but he’s such a good ball-handler, he controls the game,” Mamukelashvili said during his postgame press conference after the Kings win. “He’s got his own pace so it just kind of makes it so much easier for shooters. All you have to do is stay there and he’s gonna find you.

“Same goes with Austin. And one thing I got to say, I think everybody’s been moving the ball amazingly. Extra passes with drive and kicks. I feel like nobody tries to hold it for too long. So it’s just been fun playing.”

The Lakers signed Sandro Mamukelashvili to a four-year contract in the offseason, and he appears to have solidified himself as the team’s primary backup big man. He can play both power forward and center, he can handle the ball at times and make decision, he can shoot consistently from 3-point range, he’s a connector that can be plugged in and played with multiple lineups.

Back when the Lakers initially signed him, head coach JJ Redick recalls him asking how he best fits within the team’s system. Redick told him he envisions him as a basketball player who can fit in anywhere. And through the first few preseason games, he’s enjoyed drawing up plays that take advantage of Mamukelashvili’s skill set.

“He’s a good passer. Part of it for him is the threat of his shot. So if he has the initial action with the ball, then what comes after that when he doesn’t have the ball, he’s able to sort of get that space and then create an advantage because of the threat of his shot,” Redick said following Lakers’ practice on Oct. 10. “I’m gonna have some fun running plays and ATOs for him. We’ll have a little ‘Mamu’ package … We‘ll get creative with him. It’ll be fun.”

Mamukelashvili is coming off a career year with the Toronto Raptors in which he received votes for the Sixth Man of the Year Award. He appeared in a career-best 80 games, including 13 starts, at a little over 21 minutes per game.

The former Seton Hall standout averaged a career-high 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists with splits of 52.3 percent shooting from the field, 38.9 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 74.7 percent shooting from the free-throw line. His field goal and 3-point efficiency were both career highs.
For Doncic, who is used to be being the primary ball-handler and playmaker, Mamukelashvili gives him someone who can take some of the pressure off of him at times in that regard.

“I knew what kind of player he was, obviously I played against him,” Doncic said following Lakers’ practice on Oct. 10. “I think just his ability to handle the ball, and just see the court. Some of his passes I think are very underrated, so I think that’s the thing that’s most impressed me.”
But while the 27-year-old can handle the ball and make decisions, he’s still looking forward to the open shots he’s going to receive alongside Doncic and Reaves.

“They have so much gravity … I just imagine myself being open and making sure I knock down my 3s or get the ball and push. A lot of times Luka and Austin are denied,” Mamukelashvili said. “And also just making sure I’m the connector … make the right reads … and just kind of compliment them as much as possible.”

articles.headline: How long does it take to beat Hellraiser: Revival?
keyFacts: Hellraiser: Revival takes about 10 to 15 hours to beat, according to Destructoid.
The game offers four difficulty settings, with the Hellraiser difficulty requiring the biggest time investment due to limited saves.
Players can unlock two different endings by accepting or denying the Cenobites' offer at the end of the campaign.
body: Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival puts players on a leather-filled journey through the Labyrinth, where one wrong step can mean a very painful end.
But how long does the game actually last? Here’s how long it takes to beat Hellraiser: Revival , as well as how much time those looking to 100% it must be ready to invest.
Table of contents
How long does it take to beat Hellraiser: Revival? All Hellraiser: Revival difficulties, explained
Does Hellraiser: Revival have multiple endings?
How long does it take to beat Hellraiser: Revival?

Image via Saber Interactive. Contrary to what many might imagine, given its 69 achievements on Steam , Hellraiser: Revival can be beat in around 10 to 15 hours, even by those not used to first-person survival titles or puzzle solving in general. It might, however, take you a little longer depending on your difficulty choice, with Hellraiser requiring by far the biggest investment due to its lack of autosaving and limited manual saves.
All Hellraiser: Revival difficulties, explained

Available from the get-go, you can pick between four different difficulty settings when starting a new playthrough in Hellraiser: Revival . You can check out an overview of all of them below. No achievements/trophies require completing the game in set difficulties.
Easy : A story-focused difficulty. Enemies won’t provide a challenge or demand heavy resource management.
Normal : The game’s balanced difficulty. Ideal for newcomers.
Hard : Features harder enemies, limited save locations, and disables autosaves entirely. Perfect for those looking for a fair but steep challenge.
Hellraiser : Features merciless enemies, a higher number of hostiles, and lower resources. Saving is locked behind the use of Save Tokens. Cannot be changed once a playthrough starts.

articles.headline: A college in Illinois tried to cancel its Flock contact and it refused
keyFacts: In October 2025, Elgin Community College asked Flock to remove its safety cameras over data privacy and security concerns.
Flock refused the removal requests and ignored a later offer from school officials to pay for the remaining contract months.
College staff repeatedly covered the cameras with trash bags, but workers assumed to be from Flock kept removing the covers until the contract expired.
body: In April of 2025, Elgin Community College had six Flock safety cameras installed to “enhance the safety and security of students.” But by September of that year, the school’s administration grew concerned that Flock was sharing data with Customs and Border Patrol, that camera feeds were not properly secured, and that both law enforcement and the company’s employees were abusing access to the data.
A college in Illinois tried to cancel its Flock contact and it refused
Flock refused to take its cameras down so Elgin Community College covered them. The company snuck back to undue it.

So in October of 2025, Elgin Community College requested Flock to remove its cameras. According to Elgin’s President Peggy Heinrich, Flock rejected the request, saying it had not violated its contract. According to the Chicago Sun-Times, school officials reached out again in December, offered to pay for the remaining five months of the contract, and still requested that the cameras be removed. They were met with silence.

Heinrich said Elgin Community College staff began to cover the cameras using black trash bags and zip ties so that they would not be able to capture footage. But workers in an unmarked vehicle, which Heinrich assumed belonged to Flock, repeatedly removed the coverings.
“We were kind of in a back and forth for a bit where we’d cover, and then when they’d come to service, they’d remove,” Heinrich said. “Then we’d cover and then they’d remove.”
This continued until April of this year when the college’s contract expired, and Flock removed the cameras.

articles.headline: Polls come under scrutiny as Democrats take the lead in midterm elections
keyFacts: Democrats are leading in midterm election polls across major competitive races and several traditionally Republican states.
Analysts and pollsters said polling errors might overestimate Democratic leads because Republican voters are less likely to respond to surveys.
Analysts noted that potential polling errors could significantly impact which party wins control of Congress on Election Day.
body: With less than a month to go before the midterm elections , Democrats are doing so well that many political observers are beginning to wonder if there is something wrong with the polls .

It’s not just that President Donald Trump is unpopular, with a job approval rating below 40% nationally, though that is exactly what the RealClearPolitics polling average shows . He receives even lower marks on three of the top issues in the midterm campaign: Iran, the economy, and inflation, where he’s below 30% approval.

Nor is it just that voters prefer Democrats controlling Congress over Republicans by 7.9 points, according to the same website’s average of polls , with some recent surveys giving Democrats a lead as high as 12 points. The final RealClearPolitics average ahead of the 2018 midterm elections during Trump’s first term was a 7.3-point Democratic edge. Democrats gained more than 40 House seats that year to take the majority and ended up winning the congressional popular vote by 8.4 points.
Democratic candidate for Congress Christina Bohannan, at far right, speaks to a county-level organization of Democrats in Columbus Junction, Iowa, Aug. 16, 2026. (Joseph Cress/AP)

But this blue wave is threatening to wipe out Republicans in some of the reddest states in the country. Democrats are ahead in the RealClearPolitics average for every major competitive Senate race in the country except for Kansas, where Sen. Roger Marshall (R-KS) clings to the barest 0.2-point advantage. This includes Democratic leads in Texas, Ohio, Iowa, and Alaska, all states Trump won by double digits just two years ago.

North Carolina, which hasn’t voted Democratic at the presidential level since 2008, is considered by many in both parties to be all but gone as campaign cash is redirected elsewhere. Georgia, once viewed as the Republicans’ best Senate pickup opportunity this year, looks similarly out of reach.

Those were both 2024 battleground states that Trump won narrowly. But then there is South Carolina, which Trump carried by nearly 18 points, where the Republican-friendly pollster Trafalgar found Sen. Darline Graham (R-SC) with just a 1-point lead late last month. There has been rumbling about a couple of shock polls in Nebraska showing a surprisingly competitive race for Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE), which seems validated by Trump’s decision to campaign there.

Trump won statewide in Nebraska by more than 20 points, though 2024 Democratic nominee Kamala Harris managed to net a single electoral vote by carrying the state’s Omaha-centric 2nd Congressional District by less than 5 points.

Left: Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) arrives at the Capitol Building in Washington, D.C., for a hearing of the Senate Intelligence Committee, June 17, 2026; Right: Sen. Darline Graham (R-SC) campaigns in Irmo, South Carolina, Sept. 26, 2026. (J. Scott Applewhite/AP; Bill Clark/ CQ-Roll Call/Getty Images)

What’s the matter with Kansas — and all of these other red states? Some political analysts think pollsters are undercounting the rural vote and setting themselves up for another big miss on Election Day.

“Rural Iowa Rs ignored our survey,” election forecaster Chaz Nuttycombe wrote on X. “We think this could be a Canary in the Cornfields for Iowa polling this year.” This prompted veteran GOP pollster Frank Luntz to observe , “If Republican voters aren’t answering polls, the polls could end up making the same mistake they did in 2016.”

“We’re having problems just getting Republican voters to respond to polls,” a national Republican pollster complained to Axios late last month. “At what point do we think these guys aren’t showing up at the actual polls on Election Day?”

The polling error could correct itself in that way, with low response rates meaning low turnout — the headline on the story in which the last pollster was quoted? “GOP election outlook goes from bad to craptastic.” GOP pollster Brent Buchanan calls Trump voters who expect Democrats to win Congress “Republican Fatalists” and estimates they are 9% of the electorate.

But several pollsters the Washington Examiner spoke to said the nonresponses were more likely to produce a polling error, as some of the voters who are avoiding pollsters aren’t too demoralized to cast their ballots.

This concern isn’t just being raised by desperate Republicans, who are looking for any way out of the blue bloodbath that appears to be on the way in November — though there is, as the youths of today say, plenty of GOP cope going around. Democrats and nonpartisan analysts are preparing for this possibility, too.

“Most smart people I’ve spoken to (in both parties) think there is likely some pro-Dem bias in current polling,” Democratic strategist Adam Carlson wrote on X. “The expected size and universality of the bias varies person to person.”

Naturally, there is a lot of coping, expectations management, and worst-case scenario thinking going around. “Some of that is likely a defense mechanism from past polling misses overestimating Dems (though typically that happens when Trump is on the ballot), especially in states like Maine, where there have been large misses in the last decade,” Carlson continued. “Some of that is legitimate concern about partisan differential non-response/having a tough time reaching a representative sample of rural Republicans (i.e., not MAGA enough). … There is no way of knowing if this is a correct assumption before we have final results.”

Others have raised concerns about the “likely voter” screens used by major pollsters as the 2026 campaign enters the homestretch. “Some pollsters have a rather narrow definition of what a likely voter is, and some have a more nuanced definition,” election analyst Danny Cowan wrote . “It was with the former interpretation of a likely voter that exposed a flaw, one that inadvertently was showing Democrats to have a bigger lead than advertised.”

Before your eyes glaze over, consider the upshot of these differences. “The difference between Democrats winning by 8% or 15% is substantial. The former implies a 2018-sized blue wave where Democrats are competitive in the Senate, and the latter implies that Democrats win north of 270 House seats and 55 Senate seats,” Cowan concluded. “Democrats are very motivated to say they are voting, while Republicans are not. However, if you simply exclude those less-enthusiastic Republicans from polls, you may end up getting a sample that’s too Democratic.”

There is also the simple fact that Democrats are polling worse in blue states such as Maine, Michigan, and Minnesota than in red states such as Texas that Trump has won in each of the last three presidential elections. New Hampshire isn’t quite blue, but it has become more inclined to vote for Democrats for federal office. The Granite State Senate contest, however, is close.
This strange dynamic on its face makes political operatives working on the various Senate races across the country nervous.

Candidate quality is a logical explanation for this discrepancy. Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) is a strong candidate who has survived past election cycles friendly to Democrats, while her opponent, Troy Jackson, is weaker, though not quite as troubled as Graham Platner, the Democratic primary winner he replaced. Underfunded Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, running to replace Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX) after beating him in a primary, is not as formidable, while Democrats landed their preferred nominee in James Talarico.

Local conditions also still matter despite both parties’ efforts to nationalize the midterm elections — Republicans even took the nearly unprecedented step of holding a midterm convention at which Trump and Vice President JD Vance spoke alongside GOP candidates in some of the toughest races. The Minnesota Senate race is competitive in part because Somali daycare fraud was a big enough scandal to get Gov. Tim Walz (D-MN), Harris’s 2024 running mate, to drop his reelection bid.

Finally, three of these four Senate races feature socialists. Trump won Michigan and Maine’s 2nd Congressional District, good for one electoral vote, in 2024. He came within 4.24 points in Minnesota, the only state to vote against President Ronald Reagan in 1984. Maybe socialism is a bridge too far, or nearly so. The fourth has a former Republican senator and iconic New Hampshire family name, John Sununu, running.

If the polls are overestimating Democrats, even by a few points, this could make a huge difference in the race for control of the Senate. This is most likely in the least Democratic states with competitive senatorial elections. “In the last few election cycles, we’ve seen a pattern of Democrats looking competitive in red state Senate contests during the summer only to fade by election day,” Republican pollster Patrick Ruffini wrote earlier this year.

More than a decade ago, this kind of talk might have been confined to conservative bloggers, who were largely political hobbyists, and professional Republican partisans with their heads buried in the sand. In 2012, a plausible assumption — perhaps then-President Barack Obama would not be able to replicate his 2008 turnout and support levels from millennial and minority voters as he sought a second term, making the race closer than it appeared in many surveys — turned into an obsession with unskewing the polls.

In what eventually became known as “crosstabs truthing,” these motivated politicos sifted through the poll results and declared that the public pollsters, usually hired by universities or legacy media outlets, were systematically oversampling Democrats to the detriment of Republican nominee Mitt Romney.

Romney rather conspicuously did not win the presidential election that year. The pollsters were vindicated. But they were increasingly having trouble getting people to respond and ensuring they had representative samples, which became a major problem in the Rust Belt during the race for the White House four years later. This caused most of the polling industry to miss Trump’s upset victory over Democrat Hillary Clinton.

Nor was this a fluke. Trump outperformed his poll numbers to varying degrees in all three of his elections, including the one he lost in 2020. This was especially true in the battleground states. There was the famous 2024 Des Moines Register poll, considered the “gold standard” in Iowa polling, that showed Trump trailing Harris by 3 points in the Hawkeye State right before the election. He won by 13.2 points. Ann Selzer, the legendary pollster, announced her retirement from electoral polling shortly afterward.

In 2020, Collins trailed in virtually every poll conducted in Maine. Then she won by nearly 9 points. She was running with Trump on the ballot, losing statewide, though he prevailed in the 2nd Congressional District.

A few polls that year showed competitive Senate races in red states featuring legendary incumbent Sens. Mitch McConnell (R-KY) and Lindsey Graham (R-SC). McConnell, who is retiring after this year, won by nearly 20 points. Graham, who died in office earlier this year, won by 11.

Two years earlier, Republican Mike Braun trailed then-Sen. Joe Donnelly (D-IN) by 1.3 points in the final RealClearPolitics average, while Republican Josh Hawley led then-Sen. Claire McCaskill (D-MO) by less than a point. Both Republicans won by around 6 points. 2018 was a good year both for Democrats and overall polling accuracy. But that year, red states defied the blue wave and actually enlarged the Republican Senate majority even as Democrats captured the House. And there were still polling misses.

Some go a step further and say pollsters are intentionally producing results designed to demoralize Republicans and depress their turnout. Trump routinely dismisses polls he dislikes as “fake” and sued, without much success, over the 2024 Des Moines Register poll, alleging deliberate fraud.

This sentiment is bipartisan, however. “Campaigns try to get polls that are favorable to them and put them out … get polls of questionable accuracy, but if they look good for you, get them to have media folks pick them up and report them to try to create like a bandwagon effect, which is a technique as old as politics itself,” retiring Sen. Gary Peters (D-MI) told reporters after his preferred candidate lost the Michigan Senate primary but outperformed her poll numbers. “We saw polls that were questionable right from the start for me.” More on this later.

In fact, pollsters generally rely on a reputation for accuracy. Private pollsters, though their numbers are often selectively leaked to the public for political purposes, are counted on by campaigns to help them decide where to spend time and money. National Democrats would have surely liked to have invested some of the dollars that went to a noncompetitive South Carolina Senate race in 2020 elsewhere.

But there have been a few results this year that have aroused suspicions. The polling averages showed Michigan progressive Abdul el Sayed leading in the Democratic primary by more than 10 points. He ended up winning by 1 point. While response rate bias was likely a factor, with younger voters being overrepresented and other groups, such as older black voters, underrepresented, many of the polls that produced this big lead were actually conducted for groups aligned with el Sayed. He had previously accused the American Israel Public Affairs Committee of buying favorable poll results for his opponent.

Socialist Francesca Hong was expected to easily win the Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial nomination based on the polling. Instead, she lost by a slim margin. The polls came close to Hong’s vote share but wildly underestimated Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, the eventual nominee. Response rate bias was likely a factor here, too, but it should be noted that the field opposed to Hong was shaken up late in the race — perhaps too late for pollsters to capture what was really going on in public opinion. Hong had just endured a disastrous news cycle over woke social media posts and disliking Thanksgiving.

But an actual fake poll was released in the Los Angeles mayoral race and was touted by incumbent Mayor Karen Bass. “All previously published polling releases have been withdrawn and should not be cited or treated as genuine polling data,” the company that produced the fake poll said in a press release. “Median Strategies was created as a short-term social experiment examining how purported polling information could enter and spread through the political information ecosystem without independent verification.”

Another pollster used questionable methods to produce better results for Florida Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback, whose campaign had paid for the poll. Fishback ran a distant third in the primary, winning just 10.4% of the vote as Rep. Byron Donalds (R-FL) won the nomination.

These bad actors are far from the norm, but they do generate headlines and undermine confidence in the polls at a time when many already doubt them. Elections prognosticator Nate Silver estimates that polling bias occurred in one direction or the other in 6 of 10 elections dating back to 2008.

One thing to take away from Silver’s analysis is that the polls actually overestimated Republican support in some key races last year. Polling showed the New Jersey gubernatorial election was going to be close. Instead, Democrat Mikie Sherrill won in a landslide. Virginia Democrats outran their polling numbers by a smaller amount.

Some pollsters thought there was going to be a red wave in 2022. Instead, Republicans just barely retook the House and actually lost a seat in the Senate. A similar outcome for Democrats this year may be the GOP’s best-case scenario this year.

The polls could always prove right. The numbers showing overwhelming public disapproval of the cost of living and what Trump has done to handle the issue are well outside the realm of normal polling errors. The Trump tariffs hit red-state farmers and certain battleground states particularly hard. The Iran war has produced a spike in gasoline and diesel prices that generally bodes ill for the party in power, which has, in any event, lost House seats in all but two midterm elections dating back to 1938.

Republicans certainly aren’t acting as if they see different, more favorable data than what the public polls are showing. Trump and Vance are campaigning in red states. Republicans are spending a considerable amount of money shoring up what would normally be favorable states and districts. Republicans narrowly lost independents in 2022, which is why the red wave was more of a ripple. Polls showing the GOP getting trounced among these voters aren’t implausible.

“The party in power owns the pump, and Republicans are paying for it this year,” Buchanan, the GOP pollster, wrote in a memo. “Telling voters the economic stats are doing well will not change the weekly reminder of how painful it is to fill the tank. Republicans need a believable answer for voters on costs, especially for many of their own voters who are expecting the party to lose. It’s those voters who need to see how casting a ballot could change what they are struggling with at home.”
2026 MIDTERM ELECTIONS LIVE UPDATES: LATEST NEWS, RESULTS, AND ANALYSIS

Republicans had hoped to use favorable House and Senate maps to counteract a bad national environment in the midterm elections. They have used mid-decade redistricting and money from Trump’s vast campaign war chest to bolster their structural edge. So far, the polls say it isn’t working, and these trends tend to accelerate rather than reverse themselves in the closing weeks of a campaign.

Counting on the polls to be wrong is never a good place for a candidate or political party to be. But it is probably the least bad a bet has been since the famous “Dewey Defeats Truman” headline. We’ll see whether we get a blue wave or a blue mirage when the only poll that matters happens on Nov. 3.

body: What?! The Giants are level after trailing by 14 points in the fourth quarter and trailing for the whole game. Shocker from the Commanders defense. Can Jayden Daniels dig out the win from here?

Cleveland force a 3rd down and the Jets take a timeout to mull their options. A first down ends the game here. No bueno as Braelon Allen is stopped well short. Strange call after sending their leading receiver off the field. The Browns knew the run was coming. Punt on the way and Cleveland take over at their 20-yard line.

The Jets retake the lead as the running back jogs it in after a bad defensive play call. Braelon Allen has 110 yards on 21 carries. Screw it we’re watching Browns v Jets.

Hold the phone. The G-Men are just one score back with lots of time left to get back into this NFC East showdown. A win for either is huge considering both Dallas and Philadelphia (both 2-3) have already lost this week.

In two of the only close games Pittsburgh have just forced a turnover on downs with four minutes remaining and a nine-point lead over Indy while Cleveland get a sack then recover a fumble, also with four minutes remaining and a two-point lead over the Jets.

Keenum keeps Green Bay looking pretty with an interception to Ty’Ron Hopper. That looked promising for the Bears for a moment. Caleb Williams look like he will be back next week though. Emerging 3-2 after missing their starter for three games is not half bad.

Case Keenum is IN! A big kick-off return gives the veteran the controls and he begins with a nice gain of 23 yards then five. The Bears are 1st and Goal just like that. Easy to say with 20/20 hindsight but Keenum should have been in much earlier.

Goodnight, Chicago. The running back gets the score but this thrashing has been all about the quarterback Jordan Love. He is 21/27 for 300 yards and two touchdowns. Christian Watson with both of those grabs and 141 yards to boot.

Tyson Bagent throws his second pick of the game to Xavier McKinney. That has to be curtains for the backup in this one. He has struggled throughout and Case Keenum has been warming up throughout the second half.
Meanwhile Jordan Love unleashes another monster throw. This time it is Matthew Golden taking down a 36-yard grab. 19 yards to go for a touchdown. A field goal makes it a three-score lead.

Green Bay are close to home and hosed after Jordan Love fakes the boot out to the left while Tucker Kraft heads deep right. Love’s cannon for an arm easily finds his tight end who is wide open for the 46-yard gain. The Packers are in the red zone.
Three and out for Chicago who switch it up by rushing with Roshawn Johnson. Two attempts for one yard are not what the doctor ordered. Green Bay back on the ball at their 38-yard line.
Pittsburgh’s running back has just shredded Indy out of nowhere. After only five carries in the first half for 18 yards, he breaks off a 50-yard home run. See ya!

The Bears get a stop and the Packers are punting. Fair catch is called at the 12-yard line. Long way to go for an offense that has been struggling without Caleb Williams today. Quarterback Tyson Bagent is 9 for 15 for 68 yards and an interception. They do have 82 yards on the ground though. D’Andre Swift incoming.
First, Love tries to go long to Watson again up the left sideline but it is just out of reach. Watson is sure the Bears commit PI but the refs don’t give it.

Second, J.Michael Sturdivant scores a 43-yard touchdown on a deep throw from Love but he is dinged for a pass interference call after mashing his hand into the defender’s face just before the pass came.

And finally, Christian Watson grabs a 53-yard bomb right in the centre of the end zone near to going out of bounds. He goes up with a defender and grabs it off the Bear’s helmet and just plops down with the ball in his lap. Unbelievable.

Bizarre stop to the game as the officials don’t have any balls. Fairly crucial. When Jordan Love finally gets one in his hand he chucks it long for a 31-yard gain to Christian Watson. Green Bay are over midfield and then some.

Naughty Green Bay get pulled up on an illegal substitution. Love is sacked for the second time on this set of downs. Strange but Packers fans are booing despite their team winning and doing so fairly comfortably.

articles.headline: Man City's statement win has feeling of irrelevance with season in limbo
keyFacts: Manchester City defeated Liverpool three to zero at Anfield in their first match since being found guilty of Premier League financial rule breaches.
Head coach Enzo Maresca and player Erling Haaland stated that the team must focus strictly on winning matches and things they can control.
Manchester City await potential sanctions including relegation or a points deduction while their appeal is pending and the season remains uncertain.
body: - Published

Manchester City made what they will regard as a powerful statement in the most hostile territory against Liverpool at Anfield - but is it a statement that carries any weight during a Premier League season in limbo?
City's attention turned to on-field matters in their first game since being found guilty of 114 charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.
The fates, and fixture list, decreed it would be at Liverpool, whose fans nurse the most burning sense of injustice after finishing second to City in 2013-14, 2018-19 and 2021-22.

Their argument centres on the belief those titles could have been theirs had City not possessed the high finance of their Abu Dhabi-based owners, using it in the manner that led to them being investigated.

With this as the backdrop, City strode into this fevered Anfield atmosphere, with Liverpool fans high on adrenaline and determined to make their contempt for their rivals obvious - then outclassed Andoni Iraola's side in a 3-0 win.

On another day, in other circumstances, the manner of City's victory would have fed the narrative that this was a performance of champions, a winning marker laid down to their rivals as they hold a three-point lead at the top of the table.
Not here. Not in the Premier League's dysfunctional state.

Instead, once the predictable sound and fury had been diluted by City's composure and the swift realisation they were not unnerved by Anfield or the storm raging around the club, this was a surreal experience.

After the feast of excitement delivered when Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp presided over the greatest domestic rivalry of recent years, this was an occasion - remarkable as it seems - that seemed robbed of a sense of jeopardy by the circumstances surrounding it.

Yes, it was a statement display and City celebrated wildly at the final whistle, but will it count for anything given they await potential sanctions suggested including Premier League relegation or a record points deduction?

As Erling Haaland looked close to tears in front of Manchester City's fans, including his father Alf-Inge, and head coach Enzo Maresca pumped his fists in jubilation, Anfield's DJ slipped Fleetwood Mac's 'Little Lies' on to the loudspeakers in a final message of defiance.
Maresca said: "We knew there was going to be noise but we need to make our own noise by winning games. We need to learn to deal with the noise but the message is to win games.
"For me it's quite easy. I try to focus on things I can control. There are things that are not in my hands so I don't stress about them.
"I cannot control things outside football, so why stress? I stress about gameplan, day-by-day training sessions, but the rest it's not in my hands."

Haaland added: "For every single person part of Manchester City, every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time. It was tough. It was hard, but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone.

"It's always tough to come here. If you look at the record it's tough. With the Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp era it was tough for both teams, always has been. It was important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about. The thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do."
City have appealed against the verdict, but until the dust settles and final decisions are made, this Premier League season is in a holding pattern.
When City come to Anfield and win, especially as convincingly as they did here, it should be a win without qualification or questions.
This does not apply amid the current uncertainty.
Every victory, every league table, will come with a metaphorical asterisk until clarity and finality comes. No-one knows when this will be.
City's players did their jobs to perfection, victory secured by second-half goals from Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki. It is all they can do.
There can be no escape, however, from the cloud hanging over Manchester City because every win will carry the same rider - producing a state of inertia that is not good for the Premier League.
In the end, a day that promised huge discomfort for City ended in a stroll.
City navigated the hostile reception awaiting them at Anfield by arriving through the staff and contractors' entrance - while an inevitable febrile environment awaited them.
Even the derided half-and-half scarves were doing a roaring trade, until it was noticed the sky blue half read: 'Shamchester City - The Cheats'.
The announcement of City's line-up was drowned out by deafening jeers, while banners around Anfield carried a variety of messages.

They including 'A Generation Of Supporters Cheated', 'And After All You Really Robbed Us All' and - in a nod to the Oasis song Stop Crying Your Heart Out, written by Noel Gallagher who was at Anfield, 'All Of Your Stars Are Fading Away'.

This was all watched by an impassive City chief executive Ferran Soriano, but any notion their fans would turn on the owners was dispelled by a flag reading: 'In Khaldoon We Trust. We've Won It All', a gesture of support for the embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

City's fans also waved hundreds of inflatable bananas, an old habit when they spent time in the lower leagues in reduced circumstances. There remains the possibility they will get the chance to wave them down the tiers once more in the near future.

The first half did much to pour cold water on what started as a red-hot atmosphere, further diluted by City's second-half domination, although Liverpool's fans rammed home their disgust until the final whistle, chanting "cheat" every time their opponents passed in a lengthy period of possession.

Former Liverpool and England defender Stephen Warnock told BBC Radio 5 Live: "This needs rectifying as quickly as possible, but this isn't an easy thing to come to a conclusion. It's never-ending. It's so difficult and it's going to take so long to sort out."

He added: "The hard part is that this is a brilliant Manchester City team, but you have to caveat it and say they have done it illegally and they bought their way. You're caught in what you're thinking about this City team.
"I admire them because they're so good individually and so great, but the way it has been done and put together has not been put together correctly."
As City walked off, they were accompanied by the taunt of "You're going down" from the Kop.
City's fans answered with the trademark: "We're not really here."
This, in essence, is what makes this Premier League campaign one that might yet be rendered void. City might win the title - but who knows if they will be here next season?
As Maresca's side move into top gear and threaten to accelerate away from the chasing pack with wins such as this, no-one has a clue what their final destination will be.

articles.headline: Arrow Co-Creator Gives Glimpse At The Lanterns That Could Have Been
keyFacts: Arrowverse showrunner Marc Guggenheim released concept art for Emerald Knights, his cancelled 2020 Green Lantern series for HBO.
The cancelled series would have starred Guy Gardner and an original character, featuring the Manhunters as primary villains.
Guggenheim stated the project was commissioned by HBO in 2020 and fell apart around 2022 during a turbulent era for Warner Bros.
body: Last weekend, HBOâs Lanterns came to an end. Like the rest of the show, its resolution was composed of more emotional struggles and internal bouts than outright superhero space lasers. With the series in the rearview, Arrowverse showrunner Marc Guggenheim decided to give fans their biggest peek at “Emerald Knights,” a cancelled CW-minded approach to the Green Lantern Corps.

While Lanterns followed Hal Jordan and John Stewart relentlessly hazing each other, Knights appeared to expand the scope to the broader cast. In never before seen concept art posted on Guggenheimâs Substack, we see seven Lanterns having a last stand against some slobbering alien fiends. Among them are Guy Gardner (looking a lot more like â90s Lantern Kyle Rayner), Kilowog and what might be the back of Sinestroâs perfectly pink head. The show would have starred Gardner and an original character named Bree Jarta. While it may have little significance beyond pre-production, concepts for the two characters have a striking resemblance to American Horror Storyâs Finn Wittrock and musician Janelle MonÃ¡e.

Despite obvious visual differences, it seems Emerald Knights shared a number of similarities to what we saw in Lanterns. For one, both shows would have been set between different time periods, in fact larger ones, split between Gardner in the â80s and original Green Lantern Alan Scott in the â40s. Likewise, the primary villain would not have been Jordanâs arch-rival Sinestro but the unstoppable Manhunters, who ended up with a stronger Invasion of the Body Snatchers quality in the final product.

While tempting to assume Knights was to be part of the vast, long-running Arrowverse, the show was actually destined for the same place as Lanterns. The pitch Guggenheim developed, largely as writer, was also commissioned by HBO in 2020. A pretty turbulent era for Warner Bros. and its DC comics stars, the series fell apart around 2022 just as the ‘Snyderverse’ sought an exit. In 2024, the torch was ultimately picked up by James Gunn, now running the entire DCU, who spearheaded the Green Lantern series we see today.

With a considerably different tone and noticeably more conservative budgetary constraints, Lanterns still captured peopleâs attention with the charismatic grudge-fest between its two leading super dudes. Its loudest critics felt it lacked major fights and pulls from the comics, but if its hollow cameos and multi-colored CGI food fights they want thereâs like no shortage of those on Disney+.

articles.headline: Six senators demand Trump ‘immediately reverse course’ on Russian diesel deal
keyFacts: Six senators demanded that President Donald Trump immediately reverse a deal with Russia to supply 800,000 tons of diesel to the United States.
The lawmakers stated that importing Russian oil violates a 2022 congressional law and provides Russia with a financial lifeline during the war in Ukraine.
President Donald Trump announced the diesel agreement on Friday, which also drew criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
body: A group of Senators released a statement regarding President Donald Trump’s deal with Russia to release 800,000 tons of diesel over the next two months, demanding he “immediately reverse course.”

Senators from both sides of the aisle signed onto the statement opposing Trump’s announced deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin for Moscow to provide diesel to the United States in an effort to bring down gas prices sent upward by the Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars.

“The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course,” the senators wrote, according to the Associated Press .

Four Republicans and two Democrats penned the statement: Sens. Susan Collins (R-ME), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), John Curtis (R-UT), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), and Richard Blumenthal (D-CT). While they caucus with Republicans, it is noteworthy that Collins and Murkowski have often spoken out against Trump’s initiatives, and Tillis, who is retiring, has become more critical of Trump in his final months in the upper chamber.

In their statement, the lawmakers said Trump’s deal for Russian oil violates a law passed by Congress in 2022 that prohibits the U.S. from purchasing Russian oil in order to ensure Americans aren’t funding Moscow’s aggression toward Ukraine.

“Congress was clear: the U.S. should not import oil from Russia until it ends its aggression against Ukraine and ceases threats against our NATO Allies,” the senators said. “President Trump’s decision to allow Russian diesel imports to the U.S. runs directly counter to that law.”
Tillis on Sunday told NBC’s Meet the Press that the deal puts American lives at risk because Putin’s administration has coordinated information sharing with Iran for years.

“Let’s not forget the cozy relationship that Putin has had with Iran over the years, up to and including when Soleimani was there,” Tillis said. “So look, these are bad people hanging out with bad people, putting American lives at risk, particularly our special operators and people forward deployed.”

Some other Republicans have noted how the deal contradicts a bill signed by the president intended to honor late Republican South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham that sanctions Russia. The bill allows the president to levy tariffs of up to 100% on countries that buy Russia’s oil and gas in an effort to harm the country’s cash flow. Those buyers include China and India.
REPUBLICAN BACKLASH BREWS OVER TRUMP’S DIESEL DEAL WITH RUSSIA

Trump announced the deal on Friday and said Russia would “immediately” supply over 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and global marketplace. Russia would then release 500,000 tons in November and 1,000,000 tons “immediately thereafter.”

The deal was met with sharp criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky , who said the agreement with Russia gives the country “more money for this war, more money to inflict suffering on us, without a doubt.”

body: At least 72 workers were killed in air strikes on a disputed border area between Sudan and Egypt that targeted artisanal gold miners, a human rights group said Sunday.
The attack, south of the remote Halayeb triangle, east of the River Nile, is the second of its kind this year.
It comes amid growing concern in Egypt over large-scale displacement from the three-and-a-half-year conflict in Sudan, which has spurred a cross-border exodus.
What do we know?
The Sudan-based Emergency Lawyers, a human rights and legal advocacy organization, said the attack occurred on Saturday in rugged and mountainous territory that it said lies within Sudan.
The Halayeb triangle, which is claimed by both Egypt and Sudan, is known for mining and the gold trade, along with other illicit goods and human trafficking.
The rights group accused the Egyptian air force of carrying out the strikes.
"The repeated attacks on the gold- and mineral-rich border regions reflect a desire by Egyptian authorities to expand and assert control over Sudan's natural resources," it claimed.
Egypt has yet to comment on the strikes, but has previously admitted conducting a "large-scale operation" against illegal gold mining within its borders.
Independent verification remains difficult because of the remote location.
Death toll expected to rise

Sudan Doctors Network warned on Facebook of an expected increase in the number of casualties "due to the severity of some injuries and the difficulties in accessing medical care and essential services in the region."
One survivor told the AFP news agency there were thousands of people working at the remote site when it was hit.
"After the air strike, people scattered. Some people came to Al-Ansary [gold] market, others went in the other direction. That's why no one knows exactly how many were killed," he said.
Strikes tied to war's gold economy
Sudan's civil war between Abdel Fattah al-Burhan's military junta and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has killed more than 200,000 people and triggered a severe humanitarian crisis.
Despite backing Sudan's army chief al-Burhan, Egypt considers the war at its border a threat to its security.

The RSF has funded its operations by smuggling thousands of tons of gold from Sudan's Darfur and Kordofan regions. According to the UK-based think tank Chatham House, as much as 60% of unofficial gold exports end up in Egypt.
In June, air strikes on mining sites in the same border area were followed by a large-scale Egyptian security operation.
Hundreds of people, including foreigners, were arrested, accused of illegal gold mining and smuggling.

articles.headline: Man City breach another Premier League rule immediately after victory against Liverpool
keyFacts: Manchester City breached Premier League broadcasting rules by refusing to let manager Enzo Maresca speak to radio stations after beating Liverpool.
City won the match 3-0 against Liverpool, keeping them at the top of the Premier League table.

body: Manchester City fell foul of Premier League broadcasting rules after their victory against Liverpool on Sunday.
City were 3-0 winners in their first match since being found guilty on all charges of financial rule breaks by an independent commission.
City broke Premier League rules by not allowing Maresca to speak to talkSPORT or other radio broadcasters Getty
The club, who have appealed , were adjudged to have artificially inflated their revenue by £900million via ‘sham’ contracts from the 2009/10 season to 2017/18.
Victory at Anfield is their sixth from as many games this season and keeps them top of the Premier League table.
City breach Premier League rule with Maresca decision
talkSPORT’s chief football correspondent Alex Crook was at Anfield for the match and spoke to Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola afterwards.
However, when looking to interview City manager Enzo Maresca, the club refused to allow him to speak to radio stations.
This is a breach of rule K.207 in the Premier League handbook for the 2026/27 season.

“Each Club participating in a League Match must ensure that each Radio Broadcaster that has the right to the Radio Transmission of that League Match is permitted to interview (a) at least one Player who featured prominently in the League Match and (b) the Manager, following the League Match,” it states.
City did not offer an explanation as to why Maresca was not allowed to speak to talkSPORT.
Maresca, however, did speak to television broadcaster Sky Sports, as well as the rest of the media during his post-match press conference.
Blocking out the noise for three points
Banners that read ‘Cheats’ and ‘Guilty 114’ were seen outside and inside Anfield for the heated league clash following the verdict.
Liverpool fans booed the City players as they walked out on the pitch as they and the rest of English football await the appeal’s outcome.
City were at their very best despite the hostile reception and remain top of the table Getty
However, City had the last laugh as they left Merseyside with all three points thanks to a top performance.
Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for Liverpool in the 62nd minute as he picked up a second yellow card.
Moments later, Erling Haaland fired City ahead with a well-taken half-volley to spark jubilation from their travelling supporters.
Jeremy Doku then scored the best of the lot when he curled into the top corner before Rayan Cherki wrapped up the scoring late on.
City have scored 16 goals, conceded five and kept three clean sheets so far this season.
They are three points ahead of reigning champions Arsenal and could well be favourites for the title.
City could face serious sanctions for their rule breaches but, for now, they are loving life in the Premier League Getty
However, talkSPORT pundit Scott Minto has warned the Premier League of what could happen if City were to lift the trophy in May.
“I think it could be one of the biggest shambles in Premier League history, if they’re then found to be guilty,” he said . “But if you are Manchester City, that’s the aim, isn’t it?
“To kick the can down the road, to keep on asking the Premier League, to then go back to the clubs, to keep on spending the legal battles with it.
“Do they take it to the High Court? Do the High Court accept it? How long will that take, even if they don’t? And therefore it could go beyond this season, for sure.”
talkSPORT understands Premier League clubs have planned to write to chief executive Richard Masters stressing the importance of City’s case, inclusive of appeals.
They want it resolved this season, with any sanctions that are subject to appeal being in play this campaign and as soon as reasonably possible.

articles.headline: Robert De Niro's 123-Minute Gothic Thriller Is Officially Streaming on Netflix
keyFacts: Kenneth Branagh's 1994 film adaptation Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein is now streaming on Netflix.
Polygon reports that the Gothic horror film features Robert De Niro delivering a mournful performance as the creature.
The story follows a stranded ship captain who hears the life story of Victor Frankenstein, a scientist pursued by his vengeful creation.
body: Robert De Niro is usually associated with complex, dramatic characters who make or break a film. Travis Bickle makes Taxi Driver (1976) feel like a bleak nightmare, Jake LaMotta turns Raging Bull (1980) into a visceral study of redemption, and young Vito Corleone in The Godfather Part II (1974) adds a grounded backstory for the iconic character.

Conversely, De Niro’s turn as the detached Louis Gara in Jackie Brown (1997) sparks divisive reactions, while his more recent outings, such as Righteous Kill (2008) and Dirty Grandpa (2016), are considered objective career lows.

De Niro has also appeared in some surprising roles, such as playing the part of the monster in Kenneth Branagh’s Gothic horror, Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein. Shelley’s groundbreaking book has been adapted innumerable times, including a relatively recent (and wonderful) iteration by Guillermo del Toro. Branagh’s Frankenstein is rather trope-heavy, but it is a strange and harrowing interpretation that's worth watching, in part for De Niro's mournful performance. For those interested, Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein is waiting to be discovered, as it is currently streaming on Netflix.

The film opens with a North Pole expedition in 1794. Captain Robert Walton (Aidan Quinn) and his crew are stranded after their ship is trapped in ice, but things escalate once a cloaked man named Victor Frankenstein (Branagh) emerges and starts telling his life story. A deafening roar can be heard in the background, but the source isn’t revealed at this point in the story.

Victor relays his circumstances growing up, his background in medicine, and how he stumbled upon research about creating new life. Building a creature out of these notes, Victor is horrified by its appearance and refuses to offer it any guidance or comfort. The rest follows the basic beats of the novel. After being abandoned, the creature attempts to protect a blind patriarch, but his terrifying appearance prevents him from forming any long-lasting bonds. After learning about his origins, the creature vows revenge on Victor, and his trail of carnage begins.

At some point, the creature asks Victor to grant him a female companion in exchange for leaving him and humanity alone. Although our scientist agrees, he is unable to fulfill this demand, which leads to more gruesome tragedy.
A fantastic Robert De Niro performance

Branagh’s penchant for theatrics colors every event in Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein. This approach has worked quite well on occasion, such as his four-hour adaptation of Hamlet (1996) and his Agatha Christie whodunnits, Murder on the Orient Express (2017) and Death on the Nile (2022).

Not everyone favors such a vivid approach to a complex classic, but this high-octane intensity highlights some of the most passionate aspects of Shelley’s text. Branagh’s Victor is a man swayed by passion, which feeds into his fickle attitude towards playing god and his tendency to abandon his problems instead of facing them head-on.

There’s also the creature, who is more intelligent and world-weary than Victor gives him credit. De Niro brings a heartbreaking pathos to the role, which is a necessary component in our understanding of a being forsaken by its maker. The creature is curious about the world around him, which is reflected in his urge to understand how and why Victor created him. “What of my soul? Do I have one? What of these people of which I am composed?” he asks, taking a more philosophical approach to the act of cobbling body parts together and creating an “abomination,” as Victor so tactlessly puts it.

Every scene featuring the creature is moving, turning Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein into an adaptation that could’ve been much more consistent in tone. Victor's adoptive sister/wife Elizabeth (Helena Bonham Carter) also plays a more tragic role than in the source material, but these changes aren’t subtle enough to feel effective. Although Branagh’s love for melodrama leaves the film devoid of meaningful scares, it makes for a visually striking experience that is hard to forget. The sequences set in the North Pole are stunning, effectively conveying a sense of loneliness that both Victor and the creature can resonate with.

Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein doesn’t radically reinterpret the classic tale. But it is a beautiful, spirited adaptation with compelling performances, suited for those who long for a period drama that (over)indulges in twisted romance and melancholy.
Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein is streaming on Netflix.

articles.headline: Anbernic's next dual-screen handheld has the perfect aspect ratio for 3DS games
keyFacts: Anbernic revealed the RG DDS, a new dual-screen handheld console designed to emulate systems like the Nintendo 3DS.
The device features a 5:3 main display, a 4:3 secondary screen, a Snapdragon G2 Gen 2 chip, and a 6,000mAh battery.
Anbernic did not announce pricing or release date details for the new handheld.
body: Anbernic's next dual-screen handheld has the perfect aspect ratio for 3DS games
The RG DDS’s main display has a 5:3 aspect ratio while its bottom screen will be 4:3.

It's only been a year since Anbernic teased its remake of the Nintendo DS but the handheld company is already moving on to a contemporary version of its successor. Anbernic revealed the RG DDS, which is short for "Dream Dual-Screen" and an obvious nod to the Nintendo 3DS.

Improving on its predecessor, the RG DS, Anbernic went with Qualcomm's Snapdragon G2 Gen 2 chip. That means the RG DDS should handle emulating even up to Nintendo Switch and PlayStation 2 titles. Equipped with two displays, most gamers are likely going to replay 3DS favorites because of its matching aspect ratios. Anbernic built the clamshell handheld with a 4.7-inch main display that has a 1,200 x 720 resolution for a 5:3 aspect ratio and paired it with a 4-inch secondary display with a 960 x 720 resolution for a 4:3 aspect ratio. Anbernic hasn't revealed the rest of its upcoming handheld's internals, outside having a 6,000mAh battery.

As for the controls, the RG DDS is almost an exact match to Nintendo's handheld, but Anbernic added an extra analog stick on the right side. The dual-screen device even has an extendable capacitive stylus that can be tucked away when not in use. Anbernic also said there's a dedicated AI button, but hasn't yet detailed exactly what features it activates.

As usual, the handheld maker excluded any pricing or release dates in the reveal, but we're expecting the RG DDS to be a little more expensive than its $99 precursor. However, Anbernic is known for its affordability so it could potentially undercut the recently-released Retroid Pocket Duo and its Lite model that starts at $149.

articles.headline: Nithya Raman’s LAPD shake-up could put ousted progressive DA George Gascón in charge of cops
keyFacts: Los Angeles mayoral candidate Nithya Raman faced rumors that she might appoint former District Attorney George Gascón as LAPD chief.
Raman denied knowing Gascón personally and stated she did not know the origin of the rumors.
Law enforcement officials and union representatives warned that appointing Gascón could cause a mass exit of police officers.
body: Nithya Raman has issued a word-salad denial on whether she will make controversial former District Attorney George Gascón head of the LAPD if she becomes mayor of Los Angeles.
The DSA-backed candidate appeared to panic during a TV appearance and said “I don’t know him personally” when grilled over bringing back the ultra-liberal former cop.
It comes just a day after she issued an outright denial to The California Post on appointing him, further muddying the water on what she plans if she gains office.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.
Thanks for signing up!
Raman sparked fury last week when The Post unearthed a since deleted “fascist liars” video featuring LAPD chief Jim McDonnell with a giant red X across his face.
During her NBC appearance Sunday, Raman was quizzed on the rumors she wants to bring back Gascón, who was dumped as LA County DA during a recall in 2024 over his progressive policies.
Raman said: “No, no. I don’t know where the rumors are coming from. I don’t know him personally.”

The rumors are the latest headache for Raman, who spent much of the past week explaining a since-deleted social media video featuring McDonnell’s face crossed out with a giant red X beneath the words “Only you can stop fascist liars.”
During an ABC7 interview Saturday Raman insisted replacing McDonnell was not among her immediate priorities.
“You know, replacing the chief of police is not on my 100-day agenda. Restoring trust with our law enforcement and the public is on my 100-day agenda,” Raman said.
Pressed about Bass’ warning that firing McDonnell ahead of the LA 2028 Olympics could be disastrous, Raman suggested waiting until 2030.
“I believe his term goes through 2030, if I’m not mistaken, and at that point I think I would be looking to appoint a new chief,” she said.
But when The California Post sought clarification Saturday, Raman offered a different timetable.
“Chief McDonnell’s term ends in 2030 and I would expect to replace him prior to that,” she told The Post, promising a “careful, orderly transition.”

Raman said she did not know where the Gascón rumors originated, but multiple law enforcement and political sources told The Post his name has been circulating inside City Hall and among rank-and-file cops as a possible replacement.
The prospect has alarmed law enforcement officials, who warn appointing him could trigger a mass exodus from the already understaffed LAPD.

“Gascón would turn the LAPD upside-down,” Dennis Zine, 79, a former LA City Councilman and longtime LAPD officer, told The Post. “He basically flipped from one extreme to the other — law enforcement to pro-criminal.
“I would think you’d see a mass exodus of officers with less than five years on the job,” Zine warned. “It’s like the ship is sinking. Let’s get out while we can.”
Los Angeles City Councilwoman Traci Park also said that the choice of police chief could worsen the department’s staffing crisis.
“Decisions about leadership and the appointment of the chief and command staff is something that will absolutely directly impact our staffing levels at LAPD,” Park said.
The Los Angeles Police Protective League was even more forceful.
“Apparently, Nithya Raman’s public safety plan consists of appointing the author of Proposition 47, George Gascón, to be our Chief of Police,” the union’s board of directors charged.
“We’d be laughing if it wasn’t so frightening that after getting bounced two-years ago as District Attorney by a landslide, Raman wants to flip her nose at voters and return Gascón to power.”
Gascón, 72, has longstanding ties to LA’s democratic socialist movement, with the DSA’s Los Angeles chapter urging voters to support him in 2024.
A well-connected senior LAPD officer claimed Gascón is widely believed within the department to be Raman’s preferred replacement.

“It’s not a secret. Everyone knows that. Everyone saying that she’s in touch with him,” the officer said. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli blasted the prospect during a Skid Row press conference.

“I think when you talk to the residents of LA, they want law and order, the days of lawlessness are over,” Essayli said. “Mr. Gascón lost an election over that. So the decision will be made by the voters.”
Political strategist Michael Trujillo questioned whether voters would accept Gascón’s return.
“After voters rejected Gascón as being a public safety official as our DA, do they really want Nithya Raman to backdoor him in as being the chief of police?” Trujillo told The Post.
Gascón joined the LAPD in 1978 and rose to assistant chief before leading police departments in Mesa, Arizona and San Francisco.
He later became San Francisco’s district attorney and won the Los Angeles County DA’s office in 2020.
His four years as LA’s top prosecutor sparked bitter battles over sentencing enhancements, juvenile prosecutions and policies critics considered too lenient.
Supporters argued his reforms reduced excessive punishment and racial disparities. Voters ousted him in 2024, electing Nathan Hochman.
Zine warned a Gascón appointment could drive officers into retirement or neighboring departments just as Los Angeles prepares for the Olympics.
“You’re gonna see a lot of them leaving before the Olympics. There’s no question,” he said.
“We don’t have enough officers now to maintain policing the city of Los Angeles, let alone the drain it’s gonna take on the Olympics.”
One current Los Angeles prosecutor delivered an equally stark assessment.

“Law enforcement hates him. Voters hate him. And Raman attempting to resurrect him should terrify residents of Los Angeles who suffered under the crime spree that took place while Gascón was the DA,” the prosecutor told The Post. “It’s a massive step backwards.”
